models.title: Two compensation models that make sense

faq.title: Frequently asked questions from partner agents

items.question: What does the partnership cost?
items.answer: Nothing in advance. There is no monthly fee, no licence or software cost, and no minimum turnover. Payment is due only after a successful sale. We earn only when you sell.

items.question: Do I have to give up self-employment?
items.answer: No. You remain self-employed and organise your own work. We provide the structure, network, and transaction support. This does not create an employment relationship.

items.question: Can I promote the network?
items.answer: Yes. You may communicate the partnership and our network openly, including on your own website.

items.question: Is every property I introduce accepted?
items.answer: No. Every property is reviewed and must meet the Immonation standard. This protects quality and your time because we do not market properties that will not work in the market.

items.question: Who sets the asking price?
items.answer: We assess each property together and set a market-aligned price. This means you do not enter the sales process with an inflated price that prevents a successful transaction.

items.question: Which region do you cover?
items.answer: Our core area is the Nuremberg metropolitan region: Nuremberg, Fürth, Erlangen, Zirndorf, Schwabach, and the surrounding area.

sections.heading: § 1 Scope and contracting parties
paragraphs: (1) These terms and conditions apply to all contracts and services between Immonation GmbH (hereinafter “Immonation”) and its customers — via the website https://www.immonationgmbh.de as well as under any agreement concluded between the parties.

(2) A customer within the meaning of these terms is the seller or buyer of a property and, in exceptional cases, also the landlord or — subject to the “Bestellerprinzip” — the person seeking a tenancy. The principal contract is the purchase, rental, or lease contract brokered in each case.

(3) A consumer is any natural person who concludes the contract predominantly for private purposes (Section 13 BGB); an entrepreneur is anyone acting in the exercise of a commercial or independent professional activity (Section 14 BGB).
(4) Individually agreed terms and property-specific commission disclosures take precedence over these terms (Section 305b BGB).

sections.heading: § 2 Subject matter and formation of the contract
paragraphs: (1) Immonation provides brokerage services in the form of evidencing the opportunity to conclude a contract or brokering such a contract concerning real estate.

(2) The contract is formed when the customer makes use of Immonation’s services — in particular by retrieving an exposé or further property information, arranging a viewing, or entering into negotiations — after Immonation has appeared recognizably as broker and has quantified its commission claim for the success case.
(3) Evidencing or brokering a purchase contract for an apartment or single-family house to a consumer requires text form (Section 656a BGB).
(4) Where the parties have a separate written agreement, its provisions take precedence over these terms in the event of conflict.

sections.heading: § 3 Services, offers, and property information
paragraphs: (1) The scope of services follows the agreement in each case and includes in particular valuation, preparation of documents, marketing, qualification of prospects, viewings, and support through to the notary appointment.
(2) Immonation’s offers are non-binding and subject to change. Prior sale, price changes, and error are reserved.

(3) Property-related information regularly originates from the owner, seller, property manager, authorities, or other third parties. Immonation forwards this carefully but assumes no warranty for accuracy, completeness, or currency unless it knew or ought to have known of the inaccuracy. Checking information material to the customer’s decision is the customer’s responsibility.

sections.heading: § 4 Customer cooperation and power of attorney
paragraphs: (1) The customer provides the documents and information required for marketing completely and accurately.

(2) Under the separate agreement, the seller authorizes Immonation in particular to inspect the land register and official files and to request and receive required documents from authorities and the notary. Where separately agreed, this power of attorney continues for up to twelve months after conclusion of the principal contract for the purpose of reviewing the causality of the brokerage activity.

sections.heading: § 5 Commission claim and amount
paragraphs: (1) The commission claim arises as soon as a valid principal contract is concluded as a result of Immonation’s evidencing or brokerage (Section 652 BGB). It is sufficient that Immonation’s activity was a contributing cause of the contract conclusion.
(2) On a sale, the commission is 3.57% including 19% VAT of the notarized purchase price per contracting party (seller and buyer side), unless otherwise agreed for the specific property.

(3) If Immonation acts for both sides when a consumer purchases an apartment or single-family house, it may only have commission promised by both parties in equal amounts (Section 656c BGB). If only one party is the instructing party and a consumer, the other party bears at most the same share and only after the first party has evidenced payment (Section 656d BGB).
(4) Multiple sellers are jointly and severally liable. The commission arrangement becomes effective upon joinder of all owners entered in the land register or upon valid representation.

(5) The assessment basis is the notarized purchase price. If further valuable consideration is agreed in the course of the transaction — such as assumption of liabilities, buy-out or distance payments, or inventory sold with the property — the assessment basis increases accordingly insofar as those performances form part of the brokered transaction.
(6) A commission claim already earned does not lapse because the principal contract is later mutually cancelled or reversed; cases of initial invalidity remain unaffected.

sections.heading: § 6 Economically equivalent transactions and related persons
paragraphs: (1) If a closing results from Immonation’s activity, the commission claim remains intact even if the concluded contract differs in content from the evidenced opportunity or if a transaction with essentially the same economic result takes its place, provided that success is based on Immonation’s evidencing or brokerage.

(2) Conclusion with the customer is equivalent to conclusion by a person so closely connected to the customer personally, familially, legally, or economically that the contract economically benefits the customer. This includes in particular close relatives, companies controlled by or affiliated with the customer, and trustees or nominated purchasers engaged by the customer.

sections.heading: § 7 Due date and duty to notify
paragraphs: (1) Commission is earned and due upon conclusion of the principal contract; for contracts requiring notarization, upon notarization. It is payable after invoicing.

(2) Immonation is entitled to attend the conclusion of the principal contract. If the customer concludes the contract without Immonation’s involvement, the customer shall promptly inform Immonation of the closing and of the contractual contents relevant to commission calculation.

sections.heading: § 8 Rent and lease
paragraphs: (1) Immonation’s focus is on sales. Brokerage of rental or lease properties occurs only in individual cases and requires a separate agreement.

(2) For brokering commercial rental or lease contracts, the commission is three net cold rents or net leases plus statutory VAT, unless otherwise agreed for the property. The monthly net cold rent or net lease without operating and ancillary costs is decisive.

(3) For brokering residential tenancies, the “Bestellerprinzip” (Section 2 WoVermRG) applies: commission from the person seeking a tenancy is charged only if that person previously instructed Immonation in text form and Immonation acts exclusively on that instruction. Otherwise remuneration is agreed solely with the landlord.
(4) Remuneration agreed with the landlord is two net cold rents plus statutory VAT, unless otherwise agreed for the property.

sections.heading: § 9 Dual agency
paragraphs: In purchase contracts, Immonation may act commissionably for seller and buyer and is obliged to treat both sides fairly. When brokering residential tenancies, it may act commissionably for only one of the two sides. Mandatory statutory rules on the allocation of brokerage costs remain unaffected.

sections.heading: § 10 Prior knowledge
paragraphs: (1) If the customer already knows the evidenced property, the contractual opportunity, or the named contracting party, the customer shall notify Immonation without delay in text form and name the source of that knowledge in a comprehensible manner.

(2) Prior knowledge does not affect the commission claim if Immonation’s evidencing or brokerage was at least a contributing cause of the contract conclusion. Failure to notify or late notification may be taken into account when assessing causality.

sections.heading: § 11 Ending the cooperation; expenses
paragraphs: (1) The cooperation is not time-limited and may be ended by either side at any time with reasonable notice.

(2) If the property is marketed unsuccessfully for at least three months and the customer then ends the cooperation, no costs arise for the customer. The three-month period begins with Immonation’s first online listing of the property.

(3) If the customer ends the cooperation before expiry of those three months, Immonation may claim reimbursement of expenses actually incurred and evidenced up to that point (e.g. insertion, photo and video costs, travel costs), capped at a maximum of 25% of the commission expected upon success. The customer remains entitled to prove that no expenses or substantially lower expenses arose (Section 309 No. 5 BGB).
(4) If Immonation had no opportunity for online marketing before termination, paragraph 3 applies accordingly.

sections.heading: § 12 Private sale and withdrawal after reservation
paragraphs: (1) If the customer sells the property after instructing Immonation without first giving Immonation an opportunity to market via the intended channels, Immonation may invoice the services performed and evidenced up to that point in accordance with § 11.

(2) If a prospect evidenced by Immonation has made a binding reservation at the agreed purchase price and the customer then withdraws from the sale or concludes the principal contract with that prospect independently, Immonation is entitled to the agreed commission.

sections.heading: § 13 Continuing commission
paragraphs: If the customer concludes a principal contract within six months after ending the cooperation with a prospect whom Immonation had previously demonstrably named or evidenced, the agreed commission is payable provided the evidencing or brokerage was causal for the contract conclusion.

sections.heading: § 14 Confidentiality and disclosure of information
paragraphs: (1) Offers, exposés, and property documents provided by Immonation are confidential and intended solely for the customer; disclosure to third parties requires prior consent in text form.

(2) Disclosure remains permitted to the financing bank, notary, lawyer, or tax adviser, and to other advisers directly involved in reviewing or completing the specific transaction, provided they are bound to confidentiality and do not themselves act as purchaser or economic beneficiary.

(3) If unauthorized disclosure causes a third party to conclude the principal contract, Immonation may claim damages; the damage may in particular consist of lost commission. The customer remains entitled to prove that no damage or a lesser damage arose.

sections.heading: § 15 Liability
paragraphs: (1) Immonation forwards third-party information unchecked; checking it for accuracy and completeness is the customer’s responsibility.

(2) For slight negligence, Immonation is liable only for breach of material contractual duties and limited to the contract-typical, foreseeable damage. Liability for intent and gross negligence, for damage from injury to life, body, or health, and under the Product Liability Act remains unaffected.

sections.heading: § 16 Right of withdrawal for consumers
paragraphs: If a consumer concludes the contract by distance selling or away from business premises (e.g. at an appointment in the property), the consumer has a statutory right of withdrawal of 14 days (Sections 312b, 312g, 355 BGB). Details follow from the separately provided withdrawal information and model withdrawal form. If the consumer expressly requests performance to begin before the period expires, proportional compensation for value may arise upon withdrawal; complete performance before expiry may cause the right of withdrawal to lapse.

sections.heading: § 17 Limitation
paragraphs: Claims of the customer against Immonation become time-barred after three years unless the law provides a shorter period or a different period for specific claims.

sections.heading: § 18 Data protection
paragraphs: Immonation processes personal data under the GDPR and BDSG. Details are set out in the privacy policy on the website.

sections.heading: § 19 Final provisions
paragraphs: (1) Amendments and supplements require text form.
(2) If a provision is invalid, the validity of the remaining provisions is unaffected; statutory rules replace the invalid provision.

(3) German law applies. Place of performance and — where the customer is a merchant, a legal entity under public law, or a special fund under public law — place of jurisdiction is Fürth. Statutory places of jurisdiction apply vis-à-vis consumers.

hero.lede: Our living-area calculations and floor plans do not come from an outside contractor — they come from an engineer on our payroll. He surveys on site before marketing begins, so you give away no square metre and your buyer's financing does not stall on missing paperwork.

FloorPlansPage.answer: At Immonation a salaried engineer calculates your property's living area and produces the floor plans — in house rather than bought in. He surveys on site, determines the area under the applicable set of rules, and documents it verifiably. The result is dimensioned floor plans that portals and banks accept. The documents are ready before marketing starts, as part of our service and at no extra cost.

problem.title: Close to half of all properties are listed with the wrong living area
problem.intro: “87 m²” — where does that figure actually come from? The 1994 purchase contract? An old rental ad? The previous owner? For most properties nobody remembers who calculated the living area, when, or under which rules. And that is where the trouble starts — in both directions.

items.title: Too little area stated = money given away
items.text: Understate the living area and you sell below value. At a square-metre price of €4,900, five “forgotten” square metres cost around €24,500. It happens most often with attic conversions, conservatories, and converted lower-ground floors — because the counting rules are complicated.

items.title: Too much area stated = liability risk
items.text: If it emerges after the notary appointment that the property is smaller than advertised, you face renegotiation, a price reduction, or in the worst case rescission of the sale. The area in the brochure is not a detail — it is a warranted assurance.

items.title: Different rulebooks, different results
items.text: Under the Living Space Ordinance, areas below 1 m of height do not count at all, those between 1 and 2 m count by half, and balconies and terraces usually count as a quarter. DIN 277 calculates quite differently. Two “correct” calculations of the same flat can therefore diverge by 10 to 20 %.

items.title: No floor plan = fewer enquiries
items.text: Listings without a floor plan get noticeably fewer clicks on the portals. Buyers want to understand how they would live in the space before they book a viewing. A photographed building plan from 1978 with faded lines does not do that.

bank.title: Why banks now insist on a living-area calculation
bank.intro: There is little more frustrating than this: you have found your buyer. You agree, the price is settled, the mood is good. And then the bank arrives.
bank.lead: Banks have tightened their requirements noticeably in recent years. Before financing is reviewed and approved, the institution has to determine the property's mortgage lending value — and for that it needs solid documents: a verifiable living-area calculation and a usable floor plan. A handwritten figure from an old purchase contract or a photographed plan from 1978 no longer suffices.

steps.title: The chain reaction starts
steps.text: The bank raises queries. The buyer has to supply documents he does not have — so he asks you. You search the folder, find contradictions, and have to commission someone. Days become weeks. Meanwhile the financing application sits on hold.

steps.title: And here it gets expensive
steps.text: Rate offers do not last forever. If the process drags, the interest-rate landscape can shift — and suddenly the buyer is looking at a different monthly payment than at the viewing. For most buyers, financing is the decisive factor.

steps.title: The outcome
steps.text: The buyer walks. You are back at the start — except your property has now been on the market for weeks and prospects are asking why it is “still” available. A sale that was effectively done collapses over missing paperwork.

comparison.title: What the bank accepts — and what it does not
comparison.text: Both drawings carry the same kind of information: rooms, walls, openings. Only one of them can be checked. The difference is not the care taken in drawing it, but whether every area can be recalculated from the plan itself.

faq.title: Common questions about living-area calculation and floor plans

items.question: Who calculates the living area at Immonation?
items.answer: Our salaried engineer, Hubert Christian Mahlich. He surveys your property on site and produces both the living-area calculation and the floor plan — as part of our marketing service, at no extra cost. You do not need to commission an external contractor.

items.question: Which documents does the buyer's bank need for financing?
items.answer: For the mortgage lending valuation, banks today generally require a verifiable living-area calculation, a usable floor plan, the land-register extract, the energy certificate, and meaningful photographs. Without them the financing approval is delayed — or never materialises.

items.question: Why does a missing living-area calculation delay the sale?
items.answer: Because without a defensible area figure the bank cannot determine the mortgage lending value. Queries and re-submissions follow, and they cost weeks. In that time interest terms can shift — and a buyer whose payment suddenly rises will reconsider.

items.question: When should the living-area calculation be done?
items.answer: Before marketing starts. Measuring only once the buyer's bank asks costs valuable weeks at exactly the point where a sale is most fragile. With us the documents are ready before the first prospect calls.

items.question: Why is the living area in my old documents often wrong?
items.answer: Because the rules have changed and many figures come from old purchase contracts or rental ads. Under the Living Space Ordinance, areas below 1 m of height do not count at all and those between 1 and 2 m count by half. If DIN 277 was used, deviations of 10 to 20 % arise.

items.question: Does the balcony count towards the living area?
items.answer: As a rule at a quarter, and where the quality of construction justifies it up to a half. Details like these decide several square metres — and with them thousands of euros. That is why an engineer does the calculation here, not an online calculator.

items.question: Do you also produce floor plans when no plans exist any more?
items.answer: Yes. Our engineer surveys your property completely from scratch on site and produces modern, dimensioned floor plans from it — even when no documents survive at all.

hero.title: Standard land values in the Nuremberg metropolitan region
hero.lede: The standard land value is the official starting point of every plot valuation — but never the result. We show what the current figures mean for your property in practice.

LandValuePage.answer: The standard land value is an average location value per square metre of land, derived by the local appraisal committee from actual purchase contracts. It applies to a whole zone — not to your specific plot. Whether your plot sits above or below that level depends on shape, servicing, building rights, contamination risk, and demand.

values.title: Current standard land values
values.intro: Orientation ranges for the metropolitan region. The exact value for your address comes from BORIS Bayern or the competent appraisal committee; we are happy to look it up in an initial consultation.
values.disclaimer: Standard land values are official orientation figures per valuation zone, not a guarantee of an achievable plot price. What matters for your plot is its shape, servicing, building rights and demand.

method.title: What the standard land value tells you
method.text: The standard land value is an average location value per square metre of plot. It is derived from real purchase contracts and applies to a guideline-value zone — not automatically to your specific parcel. A corner plot with building rights for two units is a different product from a narrow residual plot in the same neighbourhood.

vsPrice.title: Standard land value is not the sale price
vsPrice.text: For houses, land often accounts for 30–50 % of the purchase price — the rest is building value. Anyone who only multiplies the standard land value is almost always wrong. We value both together, free of charge and on site.

related.title: How this connects to selling and valuation

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about standard land values

items.question: What is the standard land value?
items.answer: An official average location value per square metre of plot, determined by the appraisal committee from real purchase contracts. It provides orientation and is not a sale price.

items.question: Where do I find the standard land value for my plot?
items.answer: Via the BORIS Bayern portal or directly from the appraisal committee of the relevant city or district. We are happy to look up the value for your address in an initial consultation.

items.question: Is my plot worth the standard land value?
items.answer: Not automatically. Plot shape, servicing, building rights, and demand can move the real value up or down — sometimes substantially. Two neighbouring plots can be worth different amounts.

items.question: How often is the standard land value updated?
items.answer: As a rule every two years as of 31 December; in many municipalities now annually. The appraisal committees publish the current values.

cta.title: What is your plot really worth?

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about property financing

items.question: How much equity do I need for property financing?
items.answer: As a rule of thumb you should cover at least the incidental purchase costs — around 5 to 6 percent in Bavaria — from your own funds, and ideally a further 20 percent of the purchase price. More equity improves your interest rate. Solutions exist with less equity too — Stefan Vogelsang assesses that case by case.

items.question: Can I get financing if I am self-employed or in a difficult position?
items.answer: Often yes. Not every case fits the standard template — that is exactly what the partnership is for. Through the bank comparison and experience with demanding constellations, a solution can frequently be found. A binding answer follows once your documents have been reviewed.

items.question: What is the mortgage lending value and why is it below the purchase price?
items.answer: The mortgage lending value is the value a bank cautiously and durably assigns to a property as security. It sits deliberately below the current purchase price because the bank factors in value fluctuations. It helps determine how much of the loan is well secured.

items.question: What does the unsecured share mean?
items.answer: The unsecured share is the part of the loan that exceeds the mortgage lending value and is therefore not covered by the property. The smaller this share — for example through more equity — the better the conditions tend to be.

items.question: Do I have to arrange my financing through Dr. Klein if I buy via Immonation?
items.answer: No. A purely advisory conversation is expressly possible, with no obligation at all. You decide freely where you arrange your financing — what matters to us first is that you have clarity.

items.question: How quickly will I get feedback?
items.answer: As soon as your documents are complete you receive an initial assessment of a possible financing structure at short notice. Thanks to our fixed partnership your case is handled with priority.

items.question: What does the financing advice cost me?
items.answer: As a rule no separate costs arise for you — the financing broker is remunerated by the bank if a contract is concluded. Mr Vogelsang discusses the exact conditions with you transparently.

items.question: Is the financing advice also available to partner agents?
items.answer: Yes. Stefan Vogelsang and his team are also available to our partner agents and their clients — with the same prioritised access and fast feedback as for Immonation clients.

items.answer: We and our financing partner are active across the entire metropolitan region: Zirndorf, Fürth, Erlangen, Nuremberg, Forchheim and the surrounding area.

PropertyTour.text: Short clips show fragments. This is the complete edit from one marketing campaign: a walk-through from the front door past the kitchen, living area and staircase out to the terrace — cut in vertical format, where the first few seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.

SoldVideos.title: Sold across the Nuremberg metropolitan region
SoldVideos.text: Every clip marks a completed sale — from a terraced house in Adelsdorf to commercial land in Zirndorf. The short takes are filmed on handover day and show where we actually sell.

reasons.title: Buyers are already there — we show the property where they are looking

reach.title: Reach that works
reach.text: A good property video reaches more relevant people in days than a portal listing does in weeks — targeted at the Nuremberg metropolitan region.

emotion.title: Emotion, not a data sheet
emotion.text: Moving images, a 360° tour and a real sense of the rooms create buying interest that a photo cannot convey.

speed.title: Speed
speed.text: People who already follow react immediately. Properties often find buyers before they would even need to be listed.

discretion.title: Discretion stays possible
discretion.text: On request we market entirely without a public listing — inside the network only, so your surroundings hear nothing.

levers.title: How a single video leads to a sale
levers.text: One clip activates several routes at once — and often one of them is enough.

network.title: "Someone knows someone"
network.text: Someone in the network sees the video and immediately thinks of a person looking for exactly this — and shares or tags them.

follower.title: "That is what I am looking for"
follower.text: A follower is already searching and the property fits. No detour through portals, just direct contact.

algorithm.title: The algorithm distributes
algorithm.text: Reels and TikToks are served to people in the region who are interested in property — well beyond our own followers.

topPosts.title: The most-watched property videos
topPosts.text: Every entry links to the original post on the platform. Only property videos are listed: posts about sponsorship, partners or year-end reviews sometimes reach more people but say nothing about property marketing.
topPosts.note: View counts as reported by each platform, partly rounded, as of {date}. TikTok reports large numbers rounded (for example "44.9K"); the figures here follow that display. Follower and subscriber counts are deliberately not listed — they do not describe how many people actually watched a given property.

HandoverPolaroids.title: Every handover ends with a Polaroid
HandoverPolaroids.text: When the keys change hands, we take an instant photo and write the town on it by hand. Not a marketing appointment, but the moment a sale is genuinely complete. The pictures hang in our office in Zirndorf — every one of them stands for a family that handed over its property.

sections.heading: Right of withdrawal
paragraphs: You have the right to withdraw from this contract within fourteen days without giving any reason. The withdrawal period is fourteen days from the day of the conclusion of the contract.

To exercise your right of withdrawal, you must inform us — Immonation GmbH, Nürnberger Straße 18, 90513 Zirndorf, Phone: 0911 212 838 90, Email: info@immonations.de — of your decision to withdraw from this contract by means of a clear statement (e.g. a letter sent by post or an email). You may use the attached model withdrawal form, but it is not obligatory.
To meet the withdrawal deadline, it is sufficient for you to send your communication concerning your exercise of the right of withdrawal before the withdrawal period has expired.

sections.heading: Effects of withdrawal
paragraphs: If you withdraw from this contract, we shall reimburse to you all payments received from you, including the costs of delivery (with the exception of the supplementary costs resulting from your choice of a type of delivery other than the least expensive type of standard delivery offered by us), without undue delay and in any event not later than fourteen days from the day on which we are informed about your decision to withdraw from this contract. We will carry out such reimbursement using the same means of payment as you used for the initial transaction, unless you have expressly agreed otherwise; in any event, you will not incur any fees as a result of such reimbursement.

If you requested that the performance of services begin during the withdrawal period, you shall pay us an amount which is in proportion to what has been provided until you have communicated to us your withdrawal from this contract, in comparison with the full coverage of the contract.

sections.heading: Early expiry of the right of withdrawal
paragraphs: Your right of withdrawal expires in the case of a contract for the provision of services if we have fully performed the service and began performance only after you gave your express consent and at the same time confirmed your knowledge that you lose your right of withdrawal upon full performance of the contract by us.

PriceAtlasPage.answer: The price atlas shows the price band for apartments and houses per square metre across {districts} districts in {cities} cities of the Nuremberg metropolitan region. Each location appears as a range with a median rather than a single average — which keeps the spread within a district visible. What a specific property achieves also depends on layout, condition, specification, floor, and micro-location.
PriceAtlasPage.note: All figures are guide values, not a commitment to an achievable sale price. A reliable assessment starts with a review of the specific property.

items.title: A range, not a single value
items.text: The “from” and “to” figures cover the middle 80 percent of properties. Individual outliers in either direction are excluded so the range stays meaningful.

items.title: Median, not average
items.text: The median is the value with half the properties above it and half below. It is less sensitive to individual expensive sales than the mean.

items.title: Thin data is labelled
items.text: Districts with fewer than five analysed properties are marked as “thin data”. In the current dataset, every district is above that threshold.

items.title: What the atlas cannot do
items.text: A square-metre price does not replace a valuation. Layout, specification, floor, condition, and micro-location shift the value considerably — in both directions.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about the price atlas

items.question: What does the price atlas show?
items.answer: For every recorded district, the atlas shows a price range per square metre and the median, separated into apartments and houses. It indicates which price band a location falls into.

items.question: Why a range instead of a single square-metre price?
items.answer: Properties within one district often differ widely. A range makes that spread visible, whereas a single average would hide it.

items.question: Why is the median used instead of the average?
items.answer: The median splits properties into two equal halves and is barely distorted by individual very expensive sales. It describes the typical level of a district more accurately than the mean.

items.question: Does the price atlas replace a property valuation?
items.answer: No. The figures are guide values. A reliable assessment starts with a review of the specific property — layout, condition, specification, floor, and micro-location shift the value significantly.

items.question: Which cities does the price atlas cover?
items.answer: It covers districts in Nuremberg, Fürth, Erlangen, Zirndorf, and Forchheim, each split into apartments and houses.
